sources.citation: Post, Mark W. 2015. 'Tones in Northeast Indian languages, with a focus on Tani: A fieldworker's guide.' In M. W. Post, S. Morey & S. DeLancey (eds.), Language and Culture in Northeast India and Beyond: In honor of Robbins Burling (Asia-Pacific Linguistics 023), ch. 11, pp. 182-210. Canberra: Asia-Pacific Linguistics.
sources.note: First-hand (author's own 1,900-lexeme Tangam database): Tangam listed under 'Tone, confirmed' (Table 5, p.190); sec. 5.4 pp.203-204 gives H vs L minimal pairs (Table 21) and says no more than a two-way contrast; fn.11 p.204: tone interacts with syllable weight 'like in Apatani'. Nothing at all about word stress/accent placement in Tangam.

sources.note: Glottolog types it 'ethnographic', but the Arunachal Times launch report (held) says it has chapters on the language and oral narratives, and the CFEL activity report (held) says the Tangam data were transcribed in IPA with Leipzig glossing; a language chapter of this kind usually gives a phoneme inventory and may carry a one-line statement on tone (CFEL staff treat Tani languages as tonal following Post). Independent of Post's data, hence of interest if it states tone categories.

sources.citation: Post, Mark W., Dugbang Líípír [Lipir] & Yankee Modi. 2014 [author's ORCID record: 2016]. A Tangam Dictionary, with English and Minyong Translations [listed by the author as 'A Tangam Community Dictionary']. Gauhati (Guwahati), Assam: Bhabani Press. Community edition, 200 copies, FEL grant 2013; includes a grammatical sketch and a small collection of analysed texts.

sources.note: Glottolog record (hh 322686, listed by Glottolog as a dictionary) and the FEL 2013 grant report: 'The final version of the community dictionary therefore also contains a grammatical sketch and a small collection of analyzed texts.' Compiled from Post's tonally-annotated Tangam database (Post 2015: 203-204 gives H/L minimal pairs from it), so the sketch or transcription conventions are the likeliest place for a community-facing statement on whether and how tone is. may equally omit tone marking, as Post's other Eastern Tani materials do. Tone marks in entries, if any, would be data, not a stat…

sources.note: Glottolog record only. Earliest published linguistic note on Tangam (pre-dates Post's fieldwork by 17 years); Directorate of Research notes of this series typically give a sound list, vocabulary and sentences and seldom analyse tone, so at most a remark that pitch distinguishes some words is expected. Worth checking together with Badu 2004 when a library copy is requested.
